A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoT and parity-learning study. The main text, equations, eleven empirical figures, theoretical table, and proof and experimental appendices support reliable comparison despite appendix renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original transformer parity-learning experiments and GSM8K attention-entropy analyses in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains these original parity-learning and GSM8K analyses in Section 4 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The CoT construction, transformer architecture, initialization formula and SGD procedure are retained. V2 corrects the initialization prose to match the existing formula and expands mathematical documentation without establishing an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic parity tasks and GSM8K mathematics data. The experimental appendix is retained as Appendix C rather than B; no dataset, domain or task is added.

E2.justification: The transformer comparisons with and without CoT are unchanged. Figures 6–7 retain Qwen2-7B with and without CoT and Qwen2-Math-7B with CoT; newly cited theoretical papers are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The model configurations, learning-rate sweeps, training budgets, batch size, held-out sample counts and attention-entropy metric are unchanged. V2's explanation of independently sorted head entropies documents the existing plot rather than establishing a revised evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The depth/head sweeps, multi-pass and dataset-size analyses, and attention-pattern investigations in Section 4 and the experimental appendix are retained. No new empirical ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis is introduced.

E5.justification: Experimental run/seed disclosures and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged. V2 adds no repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests; revised theoretical probability bounds belong to T1.

E6.justification: All eleven empirical figures retain their plotted content and findings. Examples include perfect accuracy after five CoT epochs in Figure 4 and the successful 50,000-sample versus unsuccessful 1,000,000-sample training comparison in Figure 5.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 gains a restricted k range, explicit finite-precision requirements and a parameter bound compatible with the learning lower bound. Assumption 2 changes its k-range denominators from log^3/log^2 to log^5/log^4, matching Theorem 3. V2 supplies an explicit ReLU parity construction, adds softmax Lemma 32, and corrects several gradient expressions and bounds. These substantially revise the formal argument, although some added equations contain label or sign inconsistencies.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same central claims: CoT improves sample efficiency beyond expressiveness and promotes sparse, interpretable attention. The introduction's change from near-linear dependence on n and k to sequence length does not materially redefine the contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4 corrects the explanatory scope of Theorem 2 from one-pass to constant-pass training, consistent with the theorem already stated in v1. The sparse-attention interpretations, GSM8K explanations and parity-focused limitations otherwise remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 newly explains that Figure 6 sorts attention-head entropies separately within each layer for the three conditions. This clarifies plot reproduction and comparison; hardware, hyperparameters, split sizes and code-access information are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references and discussion concerning Abbe et al.'s locality/globality work, Kearns's statistical-query bounds, and Kim and Suzuki's concurrent CoT parity analysis. Section 5 distinguishes the latter's noisy-oracle GD iteration results from this paper's mini-batch SGD sample-complexity guarantees, while retaining the broader positioning.

P1.justification: V2 makes local wording and cross-reference corrections, expands explanations, adds acknowledgements, and renames the final-proof subsection. New Appendix A repeats the transformer-optimization paragraph retained in Section 5, shifting the existing appendices to B and C. Most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 4 moves from page 8 to page 9, Table 1 becomes narrower with reflowed cells, and surrounding text and equations shift. The empirical figures retain their plots, axes, legends and captions; no empirical display is added or replaced.

improvement.justification: V2 improves theoretical consistency and inspectability by aligning Assumption 2 with Theorem 3 and expanding the representation and softmax arguments. The related-work distinctions and head-sorting disclosure also improve clarity. However, reversed loss labels in Section 3.1 and inconsistent parity signs in Appendix B.2 limit the reliability gained from the expanded proofs, supporting a qualified, limited overall improvement.
